Which text organises the first-instance court (المحكمة) into sections, and which sections it lists (civil, misdemeanours, contraventions, urgent matters, family, minors, social, real property, maritime, commercial).
Whether the court is the court of general jurisdiction (صاحبة الولاية العامة) for all disputes not given elsewhere by law.
Whether a section may be further divided into chambers (فروع) according to workload.
What happens in a court where the sections have not been created: the civil section hears all disputes, and whether social (labour) matters are excepted from that rule.

What happens when a case is listed before the wrong section: referral to the competent section through the registry after informing the court president, and whether this is a ground to declare the claim inadmissible or the court incompetent (it should not be).
Whether the allocation between sections is a matter of jurisdiction (اختصاص) at all, or only an internal organisation of the court.
Which matters the family affairs section hears (engagement, marriage, divorce, maintenance, custody, visitation, guardianship, matrimonial home, etc.).
Whether the family section sits with a specific judge or composition, and in camera, and whether the public prosecutor is a principal party in family matters.
Which matters the social section hears: individual labour disputes, collective disputes, social security disputes, disputes on the enforcement of collective agreements.
Composition of the social section: a judge with employee and employer assessors, and what happens if assessors are absent.
Whether labour claims require a prior conciliation attempt before the social section (import labour-prelitigation, do not restate).

Which matters the real-property section hears: disputes on property, possession, registered and unregistered land, co-ownership, leases of residential and professional premises, partition, servitudes.
Whether leases of commercial premises go to the real-property section or the commercial section.
Which matters the commercial section hears: disputes between merchants, commercial companies, commercial leases, bankruptcy, intellectual property, etc.
Which matters the maritime section hears, and in which courts it is created.

Specialised sections (الأقطاب المتخصصة) at courts sitting at the seat of courts of appeal: international trade, bankruptcy and judicial settlement, banking disputes, intellectual property, maritime and air transport, insurance; their territorial reach.

The 2022 amendment (Law 22-13) creating specialised commercial courts (المحاكم التجارية المتخصصة): which disputes they hear (art. 536 bis), and that this is an exit from the ordinary court (import ordinary-court-exits).
Whether the specialised commercial court requires prior conciliation (import conciliation-mediation).
The urgent-matters (استعجالي) section: interim measures, the president of the court as urgent-matters judge, and urgent matters within each section.
Minors section: juvenile matters, not civil claims.
Misdemeanours and contraventions sections: criminal matters; a civil claim joined to a criminal case goes there (import ordinary-court-exits for the criminal judge).
Whether the section heading must appear on the petition (court and section named in the petition), and what the absence or error costs (import petition-formal-elements).
Whether incompetence by section can be raised by the parties or by the judge of their own motion, and at what stage.
Whether a section's judgment rendered on a matter belonging to another section is void or valid.
Mixed claims (e.g. a contract claim involving real property, or a labour claim with a commercial element): which section hears the principal claim and accessory claims.
Matters that look like court-section questions but are territorial (import territorial-jurisdiction) or administrative-court jurisdiction (import ordinary-court-exits).
Whether the court of appeal mirrors the sections as chambers (الغرف) and whether that affects the petition at first instance (it should not).
Amendments to remember: Law 08-09 (2008) original text; Law 22-13 (2022) amending the CPCA, specialised commercial courts and changes to commercial section; possible changes to article 32.
